pages.title: Document definition reference
pages.description: Describe PDF content, styles, pages and metadata with the declarative pdfmake 0.3 document definition object.
pages.markdown:
# Document definition reference

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/

## Shape of a definition

**JavaScript**

```js
const docDefinition = {
  pageSize: 'A4',
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12 },
  styles: { heading: { fontSize: 20, bold: true } },
  info: { title: 'Example document', author: 'Example author' },
  content: [
    { text: 'Document heading', style: 'heading' },
    'A plain string becomes a paragraph.',
    { ul: ['First item', 'Second item'] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

const docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageSize: 'A4',
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12 },
  styles: { heading: { fontSize: 20, bold: true } },
  info: { title: 'Example document', author: 'Example author' },
  content: [
    { text: 'Document heading', style: 'heading' },
    'A plain string becomes a paragraph.',
    { ul: ['First item', 'Second item'] }
  ]
};
```

Pass the definition to your runtime's `createPdf` method after configuring fonts. All numeric dimensions use **points** (72 points per inch). Margins use the order **left, top, right, bottom**. A content array is a vertical stack. Create a fresh object for each render; the layout process adds internal measurements and positions.

## Content nodes

| Node | Purpose | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ text: '...' }` | Paragraph or inline runs | [Styling](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/) |
| `{ stack: [...] }` | Group blocks and apply a shared style | [Stacks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/stack/) |
| `{ columns: [...] }` | Side-by-side content | [Columns](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/columns/) |
| `{ table: { body: [...] } }` | Rows, cells and repeating headers | [Tables](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/) |
| `{ ul: [...] }`, `{ ol: [...] }` | Bullet and numbered lists | [Lists](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/lists/) |
| `{ image: 'key' }` | PNG or JPEG | [Images](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/images/) |
| `{ svg: '<svg>...</svg>' }` | SVG vector content | [SVGs](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/svgs/) |
| `{ qr: '...' }` | QR code | [QR](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/qr/) |

## Document-level settings

- [Page size, orientation and breaks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/page/), [margins](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/margins/) and [sections](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/sections/).
- [Headers and footers](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/headers-footers/), [backgrounds](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/background-layer/) and [watermarks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/watermark/).
- [Metadata](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/document-medatadata/), [links](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/links/), [table of contents](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/toc/) and [outlines](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/outlines/).
- [Attachments](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/attachments/), [encryption](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/security/), [PDF/A](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/pdfa/) and [compression](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/compression/).

## Definition versus rendering options

Content and visual settings belong in the definition. `fontLayoutCache` and `bufferPages` belong in the second `createPdf` argument. Fonts, table layout registrations and resource policies belong on the pdfmake API. See [API reference](/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/).

pages.markdown:
# Document Metadata

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/document-medatadata/

PDF documents can have various metadata associated with them, such as the title, or author
of the document. You can add that information by adding it to the document definition

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  info: {
	title: 'awesome Document',
	author: 'john doe',
	subject: 'subject of document',
	keywords: 'keywords for document',
  },
  content:  'This is an sample PDF printed with pdfMake'
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  info: {
	title: 'awesome Document',
	author: 'john doe',
	subject: 'subject of document',
	keywords: 'keywords for document',
  },
  content:  'This is an sample PDF printed with pdfMake'
}
```

Standard properties:

* `title` - the title of the document
* `author` - the name of the author
* `subject` - the subject of the document
* `keywords` - keywords associated with the document
* `creator` - the creator of the document (default is 'pdfmake')
* `producer` - the producer of the document (default is 'pdfmake')
* `creationDate` - the date the document was created (added automatically by pdfmake)
* `modDate` - the date the document was last modified
* `trapped` - the trapped flag in a PDF document indicates whether the document has been "trapped", i.e. corrected for slight color misregistrations

Custom properties:

You can add custom properties. Key of property not contain spaces.

## Document language

PDF document can have custom language set via `language` property.

Example:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  language: 'cs-CZ',
  content: 'Jednoduchý PDF dokument vytvoření pomocí pdfmake'
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  language: 'cs-CZ',
  content: 'Jednoduchý PDF dokument vytvoření pomocí pdfmake'
}
```

pages.markdown:
# PDF/A

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/pdfa/

PDF/A is specialized for use in the archiving and long-term preservation of electronic documents.

PDF version 1.4 or above is required.

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
    version: '1.5',
    subset: 'PDF/A-3a',
    tagged: true,
    displayTitle: true,
    info: {
        title: 'Awesome PDF document from pdfmake'
    },
    content: [
        'PDF/A document for archive'
    ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    version: '1.5',
    subset: 'PDF/A-3a',
    tagged: true,
    displayTitle: true,
    info: {
        title: 'Awesome PDF document from pdfmake'
    },
    content: [
        'PDF/A document for archive'
    ]
};
```

Supported PDF versions (property `version`):
- `1.3` - PDF version 1.3 (default) **not supported PDF/A**
- `1.4` - PDF version 1.4
- `1.5` - PDF version 1.5
- `1.6` - PDF version 1.6
- `1.7` - PDF version 1.7
- `1.7ext3` - PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3

Subset of document (property `subset`):
- `PDF/A-1` (shortcut for PDF/A-1b)
- `PDF/A-1a`
- `PDF/A-1b`
- `PDF/A-2` (shortcut for PDF/A-2b)
- `PDF/A-2a`
- `PDF/A-2b`
- `PDF/A-3` (shortcut for PDF/A-3b)
- `PDF/A-3a`
- `PDF/A-3b`
- `PDF/UA`

Mark document as Tagged PDF (property `tagged`)
- `true` - enable
- `false` - disable

Display of document title in window title (property `displayTitle`)
- `true` - enable
- `false` - disable

pages.description: Configure qr code in pdfmake 0.3 with examples, options and usage notes.
pages.markdown:
# QR code

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/qr/

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    // basic usage
    { qr: 'text in QR' },

    // colored QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', foreground: 'red', background: 'yellow' },

    // resized QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', fit: 500 },
  ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    // basic usage
    { qr: 'text in QR' },

    // colored QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', foreground: 'red', background: 'yellow' },

    // resized QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', fit: 500 },
  ]
}
```

Properties:

* `qr`: `string` - text in QR code
* `foreground`: `string` (optional, default black) - foreground color
* `background`: `string` (optional, default white) - background color
* `fit`: `integer` (optional) - fit the output QR image
* `version`: `integer` (optional) - QR version range from 1 to 40 (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Storage)
* `eccLevel`: `string` (optional, default L) - error correction capability (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Error_correction)), possible values:
  * _L_ - Level L (Low), approx 7% of codewords can be restored
  * _M_ - Level M (Medium), approx 15% of codewords can be restored
  * _Q_ - Level Q (Quartile), approx 25% of codewords can be restored
  * _H_ - Level H (High), approx 30% of codewords can be restored
* `mode`: `string` (optional) - encoding mode, possible values: _numeric_, _alphanumeric, octet_ (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Storage))
* `mask`: `integer` (optional) - mask pattern, range from 0 to 7 (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Encoding))

pages.title: Encryption and access privileges
pages.description: Configure PDF passwords, encryption versions and document permissions; distinct from resource access policies.
pages.markdown:
# Encryption and access privileges

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/security/

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  userPassword: '123',
  ownerPassword: '123456',
  permissions: {
    printing: 'highResolution', //'lowResolution'
    modifying: false,
    copying: false,
    annotating: true,
    fillingForms: true,
    contentAccessibility: true,
    documentAssembly: true
  },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  userPassword: '123',
  ownerPassword: '123456',
  permissions: {
    printing: 'highResolution', //'lowResolution'
    modifying: false,
    copying: false,
    annotating: true,
    fillingForms: true,
    contentAccessibility: true,
    documentAssembly: true
  },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

PDF document allow you to encrypt the PDF file and require a password when opening the file,
and/or set permissions of what users can do with the PDF file.

To enable encryption set user password in `userPassword` (string value). The PDF file will
be encrypted when a user password is provided, and users will be prompted to enter the password
to decrypt the file when opening it.

To set access privileges for the PDF file, you need to provide an owner password in `ownerPassword` (string value)
and object `permissions` with permissions. By default, all operations are disallowed.
You need to explicitly allow certain operations.

Following settings are allowed in `permissions` object:

- `printing` - whether printing is allowed. Specify `"lowResolution"` to allow degraded printing, or `"highResolution"` to allow printing with high resolution
- `modifying` - whether modifying the file is allowed. Specify `true` to allow modifying document content
- `copying` - whether copying text or graphics is allowed. Specify `true` to allow copying
- `annotating` - whether annotating, form filling is allowed. Specify `true` to allow annotating and form filling
- `fillingForms` - whether form filling and signing is allowed. Specify `true` to allow filling in form fields and signing
- `contentAccessibility` - whether copying text for accessibility is allowed. Specify `true` to allow copying for accessibility
- `documentAssembly` - whether assembling document is allowed. Specify `true` to allow document assembly

You can specify either user password, owner password or both passwords.
Behavior differs according to passwords you provides:

- When only user password is provided,
  users with user password are able to decrypt the file and have full access to the document.
- When only owner password is provided,
  users are able to decrypt and open the document without providing any password,
  but the access is limited to those operations explicitly permitted.
  Users with owner password have full access to the document.
- When both passwords are provided,
  users with user password are able to decrypt the file
  but only have limited access to the file according to permission settings.
  Users with owner password have full access to the document.

Note that PDF file itself cannot enforce access privileges.
When file is decrypted, PDF viewer applications have full access to the file content,
and it is up to viewer applications to respect permission settings.

To choose encryption method, you need to specify PDF version by `version`.
The best possible encryption method for PDF version is used.


> **Note:** PDF version is used only for encryption method, all other PDF elements are in version 1.3.


Available versions:

- `1.3` - PDF version 1.3 (default), 40-bit RC4 is used
- `1.4` - PDF version 1.4, 128-bit RC4 is used
- `1.5` - PDF version 1.5, 128-bit RC4 is used
- `1.6` - PDF version 1.6, 128-bit AES is used
- `1.7` - PDF version 1.7, 128-bit AES is used
- `1.7ext3` - PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3, 256-bit AES is used

When using PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3, password is truncated to 127 bytes of its UTF-8 representation.
In older versions, password is truncated to 32 bytes, and only Latin-1 characters are allowed.

# Supported Node.js versions

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/supported-nodejs-versions/

## Engine requirement

The 0.3.12 package declares **Node.js >=20** in `package.json`. The proposed CI matrix covers Node.js 20, 22 and 24 on Linux, Windows and macOS. Compatibility coverage is separate from upstream Node.js security support.

Use a Node.js release that is still maintained for production. Consult the [official Node.js release schedule](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule) before choosing a runtime. Test your own fonts, resources and document workload on the exact version you deploy.

pages.title: API at a glance
pages.description: Find configuration methods, rendering options and output helpers for the pdfmake 0.3 Node.js and browser APIs.
pages.markdown:
# API at a glance

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/

## Configure once, render many

Both entry points expose a singleton. Configure fonts, policies and layouts at application startup. Do not replace shared configuration while concurrent requests are rendering.

| Method | Runtime | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addFonts(fonts)` | Both | Merge font families; a supplied family replaces the previous family mapping |
| `setFonts(fonts)` | Both | Replace the whole font map |
| `clearFonts()` | Both | Clear registered fonts |
| `addTableLayouts(layouts)` | Both | Merge named layout functions |
| `setTableLayouts(layouts)` | Both | Replace named layouts |
| `clearTableLayouts()` | Both | Clear custom layouts |
| `setProgressCallback(callback)` | Both | Receive rendering progress; not a page-layout profiler |
| `setUrlAccessPolicy(callback)` | Both, since 0.3.6 | Allow resource URLs only when callback returns `true` synchronously |
| `setLocalAccessPolicy(callback)` | Node, since 0.3.8 | Allow local resources only when callback returns `true` synchronously |
| `addVirtualFileSystem(vfs)` | Browser | Add base64 font/resource data to the virtual filesystem |
| `addFontContainer(container)` | Browser | Register a packaged font container |

## Render

`createPdf(docDefinition, options?)` accepts objects and returns an output wrapper. Use [document fields](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/) in the first argument and [render options](/docs/0.3/options/) in the second.

| Output | Node | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getBuffer()`, `getBase64()`, `getDataUrl()`, `getStream()` | Yes | Yes |
| `write(filename)` | Yes | No |
| `download(filename?)`, `open(window?)`, `print(window?)`, `getBlob()` | No | Yes |

All output helpers return Promises. Always handle rejection. The `createPdf` wrapper itself is not a Promise. See [Node methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/methods/) and [browser methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/) for lifecycle details.

pages.title: Contributing and source architecture
pages.description: Navigate the pdfmake rendering pipeline, add focused regression tests, and validate library or documentation contributions locally.
pages.markdown:
# Contributing and source architecture

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/contributing/

## Source map

The library and this site have separate repositories:

- [bpampuch/pdfmake](https://github.com/bpampuch/pdfmake): engine, bundles, tests and examples.
- [pdfmake/docs](https://github.com/pdfmake/docs): this versioned developer site and documentation tools.

The library's Node entry is `src/index.js`; common configuration lives in `src/base.js`. Browser integration lives in `src/browser-extensions/`. `Printer` prepares resources and creates PDFKit output. `DocPreprocessor` normalizes nodes, `DocMeasure` and `TextInlines` measure them, `LayoutBuilder` and `TableProcessor` paginate them, and `Renderer` writes PDFKit drawing instructions.

## Validate engine changes

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run build:examples
npm run test:package
```

`npm test` builds generated Node and browser artifacts, then runs Mocha and ESLint. Unit tests import compiled `js/`, so rebuild after editing `src/`. Do not edit `js/` or `build/` directly. The new package smoke test installs the actual tarball in a temporary consumer with production dependencies, then exercises Node output and both browser bundles. It does not replace testing in real browsers.

Preserve text, font metrics, style inheritance and pagination when optimizing. Add an edge-case regression and, when possible, a comparison with the previous behavior. Keep a performance benchmark separate from correctness gates.

## Validate documentation changes

Use Node >=24.11 and Hugo **0.168.0**. From this repository:

```sh
npm ci
npm run docs:generate
npm test
npm run build
npm run dev
```

Open the address printed by Hugo. Generation produces the website search index, Markdown exports and MCP corpus from `content/`. Tests check metadata, examples and MCP behavior. The build verifies generated internal links and fragment targets. Commit regenerated outputs alongside source edits so clients can use the corpus without installing Hugo.

## Releases

The library retains its upstream GitHub Release trigger. The proposed workflow checks tag/version agreement, builds, tests, generates examples, tests a packed consumer, then publishes that same tarball with provenance. No registry publication happens when running local tests.

The docs workflow builds and uploads a review artifact on pushes and pull requests; it does not overwrite the versioned production site. That site's existing multi-version publishing arrangement must be coordinated with maintainers before changing deployment.

pages.markdown:
# LLM and MCP integration

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/llm-and-mcp/

## Use documentation without MCP

Every page is available as generated Markdown. The same source produces:

- [llms.txt](/docs/0.3/llms.txt): page index with descriptions and Markdown links.
- [llms-full.txt](/docs/0.3/llms-full.txt): the complete versioned Markdown corpus.
- [docs-index.json](/docs/0.3/docs-index.json): page IDs, titles, descriptions, source URLs and full Markdown.

These are discovery aids, not a search-engine or model-indexing guarantee. Keep the installed library version in your prompt. Ask the model to cite the page and use Promise output methods. The library's `AGENTS.md` explains its source pipeline and test commands to coding agents.

## Run the local MCP server

Clone the documentation repository, install its dependencies, generate the corpus and start the server:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pdfmake/docs.git
cd docs
npm ci
npm run docs:generate
node mcp/server.mjs
```

This server is part of the local improvement branch until accepted upstream. Start it through your MCP client's stdio configuration, using absolute paths:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pdfmake-docs": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/docs/mcp/server.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the example path with your clone's path. On Windows JSON paths must use `/` or escaped `\\`. Client configuration locations vary. The server writes protocol messages to stdout and errors to stderr. It does not require an API key, model account or network connection after dependency installation.

## Tools and resources

| Capability | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search_docs` | `query`, optional `limit` (1–10), optional `language` | Ranked pages with exact IDs, language, version, source URLs and excerpts |
| `get_doc` | Exact `id` from search | Complete Markdown page |
| MCP resources | `pdfmake://docs/0.3/<id>` | The same versioned Markdown page |

The server can only read its bundled documentation corpus. It cannot render PDFs, evaluate code, read caller-selected filesystem paths or browse remote URLs. Re-run generation and restart it after editing documentation.

`language` accepts `en` (default), `de`, `fr`, `es` and `pt-br`. Every supported language contains the same complete set of documentation pages. Search never silently mixes languages. A translated ID such as `de/learn/first-pdf` can be read with `get_doc` or the resource `pdfmake://docs/0.3/de/learn/first-pdf`. Each language also has its own discovery files, for example `/docs/0.3/de/llms.txt` and `/docs/0.3/de/llms-full.txt`.

## Suggested prompt

> I use pdfmake 0.3.x in Node.js. Search the matching documentation before generating code. Use the Node singleton API, register fonts, configure synchronous resource policies, await output, and cite the page IDs used. Build a fresh document definition per request.

pages.title: Performance and memory
pages.description: Measure pdfmake layout and output costs, reduce repeated resources, and control concurrency without changing document behavior.
pages.markdown:
# Performance and memory

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/performance/

## Measure your workload

Benchmark representative documents with the same Node version, fonts and input data. Record median and tail latency, peak memory, page count and output size. Separate cold startup/font loading from repeated renders. Compare table-heavy, long-text and image-heavy documents separately.

**JavaScript**

```js
const start = performance.now();
const bytes = await pdfmake.createPdf(makeFreshDefinition()).getBuffer();
console.log({ milliseconds: performance.now() - start, bytes: bytes.length });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const start = performance.now();
const bytes = await pdfmake.createPdf(makeFreshDefinition()).getBuffer();
console.log({ milliseconds: performance.now() - start, bytes: bytes.length });
```

`makeFreshDefinition()` is your own factory. Do not reuse a definition already mutated by layout. Verify text, page counts and representative rendered pages as well as speed.

## Reduce avoidable work

- Put repeated images in the `images` dictionary and reference them by key. Resize large source images before embedding them; display dimensions do not reduce the original payload.
- Prefer fixed widths when your layout permits them. Content-driven `auto` widths require text measurement; benchmark before redesigning tables.
- Register fonts once. In browser applications, ship only needed font families and variants.
- Keep `fontLayoutCache` enabled unless a measured compatibility problem requires disabling it. See [render options](/docs/0.3/options/).
- Avoid base64 when your API can return binary PDF bytes. Base64 represents each three bytes with four characters and also allocates a string.
- Use `write()` or direct stream consumption to avoid the additional concatenated Buffer produced by `getBuffer()` when you only need a file or stream. Layout still occurs before output consumption.

## Control concurrency

More simultaneous PDF jobs can increase memory use and event-loop delay. Bound concurrent renders and load-test throughput rather than only measuring one request. Use worker threads or separate processes when blocking work affects API responsiveness. Keep mutable singleton configuration out of per-request code.

## Library development benchmark

The library improvement branch includes `npm run benchmark:text` after `npm run build:node`. It compares text-array flattening with the previous algorithm using deterministic mixed input and verifies equivalent results. The optimized loop avoids repeated prefix copying. Its speedup measures that helper only; it is not a claim about total PDF generation time.

Timing thresholds are deliberately excluded from CI because shared runners are noisy. Use correctness tests as gates and retain benchmark results with environment details for review.

pages.title: Playground guide
pages.description: Explore pdfmake examples with a code editor, direct PDF preview, page navigation, local imports and downloadable source.
pages.markdown:
# Playground guide

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/playground/

## Learn by editing

Open the [playground](/docs/0.3/playground/), choose an example and edit the definition
in the left panel. The right panel shows a real PDF rendered through PDF.js.
With **Live preview** enabled, the PDF updates automatically after editing. Select **Run** or press **Ctrl/Command + Enter** for an immediate update.

The CodeMirror 6 editor includes syntax highlighting, line numbers, bracket matching, indentation, Undo/Redo buttons, persistent undo history and syntax diagnostics with line and column. Go to error focuses the offending source location. It also provides completions. Use **Ctrl + Space** to request completions. Suggested field names
are hints; the document reference defines the valid context, type and values.

## Examples

| Example | Explore |
| --- | --- |
| [First document](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=welcome) | Text, spacing and font styles |
| [Invoice](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=invoice) | A table, totals and a page-number footer |
| [Tables](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=tables) | Repeating headers across multiple pages |
| [Text styles](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=styles) | Named styles and inline overrides |
| [Columns](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=columns) | Side-by-side blocks and stacks |
| [Spans](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=spans) | Row and column spans with placeholders |
| [Pages](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=pages) | Page breaks, headers and footers |
| [Vectors](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=vectors) | Embedded SVG and QR codes |
| [Images](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=images) | Embedded PNG data reused by name |
| [Lists](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=lists) | Numbered lists, bullets and links |

An `example` URL parameter selects a known example; it does not accept JavaScript.
Live preview also updates restored workspaces, saved documents and imported files.
Turn **Live preview** off before importing code you want to inspect first.

## Preview and output

Use the arrow buttons to change pages and the zoom menu to change scale. **Page
text** exposes text extracted from the current PDF page for inspection and assistive
technology. **Open PDF** opens the generated file separately; **Download PDF** saves
the same PDF bytes. The footer shows generation time and output size. Generation
time excludes PDF.js preview rendering.

Live preview waits 650 ms after the last edit, then renders in a fresh worker. The old PDF stays visible until the next page has finished rendering off screen; the canvas is then replaced in one step. The selected PDF page and zoom are retained where possible. Downloads are disabled while the visible PDF does not match the current code. Errors keep the last successful preview instead of replacing it with a blank panel.

## Keep your work

**Export code** downloads the current definition as JavaScript. **Import .js** reads
a local file. Files are limited to 500 KB. Disable **Live preview** before importing
code you want to review before running it. Resetting or changing examples asks before replacing edits.

**The current workspace is autosaved locally**, including the definition, editor selection, undo history, example, page and zoom settings. Reloading restores the editor, its Undo/Redo history and the Live preview preference. If Live preview is enabled, the restored PDF renders automatically and subsequent edits update it without pressing Run. If disabled, rendering stays manual, including after a reload.

Give the document a name and choose **Save document** to keep a separate local document. Choosing a new name creates another saved document; saving under the same selected name updates it. The saved-documents menu restores a document and its history. Delete removes that named copy while retaining the current editor contents. Up to 30 named documents can be kept. Browser storage quotas still apply.

**Save draft locally** remains a separate quick snapshot with Restore/Clear controls. **Clear workspace autosave** removes the current autosave and pauses it until you type again. Named documents and quick drafts are separate. If browser storage is disabled or full, the editor still works and code export remains available. No source or PDF is uploaded by this application.

## Rendering boundaries

Each render starts a fresh browser worker. **Cancel** terminates it, including a
blocked JavaScript loop. A ten-second limit stops unexpectedly expensive work.
Simplify large documents or test them in a controlled application when they exceed
the playground limit. The PDF API denies remote URL resources here; use embedded
images and the supplied Roboto fonts.

Custom JavaScript is trusted user code, not a security sandbox. Do not run code from
an unknown source. A worker protects the UI from blocking but is not an isolation
boundary for hostile code. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/)
for production API guidance.

## Run the standalone development tool

From a built pdfmake library checkout, run `npm run playground`. This serves the
same UI with that checkout's engine at `http://127.0.0.1:1234/playground/`. It needs
Node >=22.13 for its separate tooling. The published library's runtime requirement
remains Node >=20. The docs site can also preview a local engine using
`PDFMAKE_SOURCE`; see the documentation repository README.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Diagnose common pdfmake 0.3 failures involving imports, fonts, tables, promises, browser windows and resource access.
pages.markdown:
# Troubleshooting

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/

## Start with version and runtime

Run `npm ls pdfmake` and compare your import to the appropriate quickstart. A browser bundle and the Node entry expose different output helpers. Version 0.1/0.2 examples using `new PdfPrinter(...)` or callbacks do not describe the 0.3 API.

| Symptom | Check | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Font family or variant is not defined | Family name, bold/italic mapping, default font | Register all used variants and select the family in `defaultStyle` |
| File not found or access denied | Actual resolved font/image path and policy | Use existing application-owned paths and a matching synchronous policy |
| Missing or incorrect glyphs | Selected font's glyph coverage | Embed a font covering the language; test bold and italic too |
| Empty or malformed table | `body`, row lengths and spans | Supply nonempty consistent rows and placeholders for spanned cells |
| `download` is not a function on Node | Imported runtime | Use `write` or `getBuffer` on the Node entry |
| Browser opens no window | User gesture and popup blocker | Open a window directly on click before asynchronous data loading |
| URL is denied despite an allow callback | Callback return type | Return literal boolean `true` synchronously; remove `async` |
| HTTP image request fails | URL, policy, CORS, status and redirects | Check access in the target runtime; browsers enforce CORS |
| File is incomplete or missing | Rejected Promise and writable errors | Await `write()` and handle its rejection before reporting success |
| Output changes after an upgrade | Version, fonts, inputs and defaults | Reproduce with a pinned version and compare extracted text, page counts and rendered pages |

## Reduce the definition

Start with one plain paragraph and known-good fonts. Add your styles, table rows and resources one at a time. Construct a fresh definition per attempt. Keep request and resource errors separate from layout errors.

## Report a useful bug

Include the exact pdfmake and Node/browser versions, operating system, a minimal runnable definition, font setup, expected versus actual behavior and the full relevant stack trace. Remove private content and secrets. For pagination defects include the smallest input that still reproduces the page break.

pages.markdown:
# Start here

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/learn/

## Start with one working document

You do not need to learn the whole document reference first. Follow these three steps:



- [1. Make your first PDF](/docs/0.3/learn/first-pdf/): Understand the definition, load fonts and run one complete example.


- [2. Learn the document model](/docs/0.3/learn/document-model/): Know when to use a paragraph, inline text, a stack, columns or a table.


- [3. Read errors and fix the right thing](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/): Separate JavaScript syntax, document structure, resources and output.



## Which runtime do I need?

| Choose | When | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Node.js](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/) | Your API or background job creates the file | `write()` for files; `getBuffer()` for HTTP responses |
| [Browser](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/) | The user creates the document on their device | `download()`, `open()`, `print()` or `getBlob()` |

The document definition is shared. Font loading and output helpers depend on the runtime.
These pages target **0.3.x**; older examples using `new PdfPrinter(...)` and callback
output belong to [0.1/0.2](/docs/0.3/migration-from-0.1/).

## Learn by seeing the result

Examples in this learning path show the exact JavaScript definition beside a real
generated PDF. Open them in the playground to edit them. Their complete source is
also included in the [Markdown corpus](/docs/0.3/llms-full.txt), including the code
otherwise generated by the interactive example components.

pages.markdown:
# Rendering options

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/options/

## Pass options to createPdf

**JavaScript**

```js
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, {
  fontLayoutCache: true,
  bufferPages: false
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, {
  fontLayoutCache: true,
  bufferPages: false
});
```

The options object is separate from the [document definition](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/).

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fontLayoutCache` | boolean | `true` | Enable PDFKit's font layout cache |
| `bufferPages` | boolean | `false` | Keep PDFKit pages buffered rather than flushing them immediately |

Keep defaults unless your use case requires a change. Page buffering can increase memory use. It does not make pdfmake's own layout lazy or incremental. See [performance](/docs/0.3/guides/performance/) and [PDFKit's page buffering documentation](https://pdfkit.org/docs/getting_started.html).

Fonts, named table layouts and resource policies are configured on the [public API](/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/). Paper size, margins and content belong in the definition.
